key_concepts: Rocks break down through forces such as man, plants, weather elements, animals, and water
Mechanical weathering is the physical breaking down of rocks
Chemical weathering changes rocks through chemical processes
Erosion can be identified by visible evidence in the environment
Flowing water from higher to lower areas carries topsoil
Erosion exposes denser rocks and pebbles beneath soil
Dry soil easily crumbles and breaks into small particles
Wind can blow dust from dry eroded soil
Terracing on hillsides prevents soil from moving downhill
Contour plowing around a hill helps prevent soil erosion
Strip cropping uses alternate strips of different crops to reduce erosion
Riprap uses arranged big stones to form a protective wall on a slope
